items.claim: C1 — Status and fidelity of the Lean statements
items.objection: The formal statements faithfully express the monic question. [N5 Frequency.lean](/Users/jinleic/jinleic-workspace/scratch/ai4s-robust-spr-interval-synthesis/quintic-spr-proof/Lean/SPR/N5/Definitions/Frequency.lean:48), lines 48–50, and [N6 Frequency.lean](/Users/jinleic/jinleic-workspace/scratch/ai4s-robust-spr-interval-synthesis/sextic-spr-proof/Lean/SPR/N6/Definitions/Frequency.lean:59), lines 59–61, quantify over every robustly Hurwitz closed coefficient box and require one real numerator with natDegree exactly 5 or 6. Endpoint ordering uses ≤, permitting degeneracy; FrequencySPR quantifies over every real frequency. Hurwitz is correctly defined by strictly negative real parts of all complex roots (N5 Basic.lean:21–22; Common/Hurwitz.lean:13–14). Main.lean:21–26 for N5 and Main.lean:30–31 for N6 assert these unrestricted targets. However, static inspection does not establish successful elaboration or kernel checking. The supplied sources also cannot establish a comprehensive current-literature claim that every individual degree n ≥ 7 is open, or independently authenticate the stated commit hashes.
items.fix: Say: 'The monic result is classical through degree four. The supplied manuscripts announce affirmative degree-five and degree-six theorems, accompanied by Lean sources whose statements faithfully match the question, including exact numerator degree and degenerate intervals. Their builds have not been independently reproduced here. No degree n ≥ 7 interval theorem is established by the reviewed material; the all-orders question remains unresolved in this audit.' Describe the source scan as finding no project proof-placeholder or proof-bypass declarations, rather than treating it as a completed kernel audit.

items.objection: The algebraic lemma is correct: theory.md:54–62 gives Σ μ_i P_{a_i,β}(t_i) = c Σ η_i H(t_i) = 0, with μ_i > 0 and deg H ≤ n−1. The explanatory phase statement at [theory.md:47](/Users/jinleic/jinleic-workspace/ai4s/robust-spr-interval-synthesis/work/theory.md:47), lines 47–49, is false when t_1 = 0: (B1) then forces E_b(0) = 0, so b(j0) = 0 and Im(b(j0) conj(a_1(j0))) = 0, not the asserted nonzero sign. Remark (3), lines 71–73, also assumes that b itself is a common SPR numerator, which contradicts its zero pairings in (B1).
items.fix: Retain the weighted divided-difference proof. Restrict the ±90-degree interpretation to positive nodes. Replace Remark (3) by: 'If β satisfied all the strict pairings, (B1) would force H(t_i) to alternate in sign, giving at least n distinct zeros between the nodes, contrary to deg H ≤ n−1.' State that this is a sufficient obstruction; necessity for arbitrary-order synthesis failure has not been proved here.

Retain [theory.md:77](/Users/jinleic/jinleic-workspace/ai4s/robust-spr-interval-synthesis/work/theory.md:77), lines 77–84. Unit coefficient normalization preserves positivity, the limit remains nonzero, and pointwise passage to the limit suffices; uniform convergence over the unbounded frequency axis is unnecessary. In the consequence at lines 86–90, explicitly require the proposed marginal box to lie in the closure of robustly Hurwitz boxes. A closed-infeasible box outside that closure supplies no stable counterexample. The grid implication requires certified infeasibility of a valid relaxation, not merely a floating-point solver report.

items.claim: C4 — Proposition D, fully closed marginal boxes
items.objection: The equivalence at [theory.md:94](/Users/jinleic/jinleic-workspace/ai4s/robust-spr-interval-synthesis/work/theory.md:94), lines 94–97, omits the Hermite–Biehler sign condition. For the monic singleton a(s) = (s−1)^6, E_a has roots 7−4√3, 1, 7+4√3 and O_a has roots 1/3, 3. These positive roots alternate exactly as asserted, but every denominator root is +1. Thus root-band order alone does not imply Hurwitz stability. Lines 103–108 additionally need nondegenerate, positive, distinct contact nodes and full-degree endpoint parts; arbitrary boundary limits can have collapsed bands or degree loss. Finally, line 110 suppresses the odd scales: the sextic paper uses hU and kV as auxiliary bounds in (3.7), and U and mV in (4.15). They are not generally the original coefficient endpoints.
items.fix: Add the correct sign orientation, for example E_±(0) > 0 and O_±(0) > 0 together with full degrees and simple positive endpoint roots. Restrict the tiling/contact statement to the explicitly parameterized nondegenerate class with 0 < x_0 < … < x_{n−1}. Within that class, the endpoint assignment, nonnegative coefficient-width criterion, and derivative equation (106) are valid. Handle collapsed bands separately. For n = 6 identify x = (a,A,B,b,c,C); the contact nodes agree with paper (4.16), while the odd factors correspond to scaled auxiliary bounds. Counting n−2 equations does not itself prove rank n−2 or a three-dimensional nullspace.

items.claim: C5 — Proposition E, reduction of non-monic boxes
items.objection: The reduction is mathematically correct, but [theory.md:115](/Users/jinleic/jinleic-workspace/ai4s/robust-spr-interval-synthesis/work/theory.md:115), lines 115–118, only explicitly proves the affine reduction of the frequency pairings. If robust Hurwitz stability of K′ is not assumed beforehand, the reverse implication also needs an argument establishing stability at intermediate leading coefficients. Moreover, '(α/β_n)B' means scaling the lower-coefficient vectors while keeping the leading coefficient equal to one; literal multiplication of the polynomials would destroy monicity.
items.fix: Define the two normalized faces explicitly as {s^n + Σ d_i s^{n−i}: d ∈ B_0/α} and {s^n + Σ d_i s^{n−i}: d ∈ B_0/β_n}. Add: a common SPR numerator on both faces gives positive pairings throughout every intervening segment. Hence no denominator can acquire an imaginary-axis zero; with positive leading coefficient and a Hurwitz endpoint, root continuity gives Hurwitz stability throughout. The conclusion that separate monic existence theorems do not automatically supply a common numerator for both faces is correct.

items.objection: The blanket 'all had a grid-feasible closed problem' is not established by successful optimization when 632 optimal margins were negative. Rechecking 40 cases leaves 592 negative cases unrechecked. 'Rechecked in 60-digit arithmetic' overstates the computation: [closed_exact3.py:136](/Users/jinleic/jinleic-workspace/ai4s/robust-spr-interval-synthesis/work/closed_exact3.py:136) converts the normalized rows to float; lines 140–155 use double-precision SciPy/NumPy optimization. Only reconstruction and nullspace computation use multiprecision. The recheck also removes the original nonnegative-coefficient restriction, so a changed outcome cannot be attributed solely to conditioning without checking the returned numerator against the original formulation. Numerical root tests in sprlib.py:67–79 do not certify robust stability. The inspected permitted evidence does not corroborate the stated batch totals.
items.fix: Strongest defensible wording: 'No certified counterexample was obtained in the reported searches. The reported 400 monic samples per degree n = 5,6,7,8 had positive estimated finite-grid angular margins; the reported non-monic samples at n = 3,4,5 also passed the numerical grid tests. The boundary walks tested the reported numbers of states, with 632 negative restricted-LP margins at n = 10,11. For 40 selected cases, 60-digit reconstruction of the contact space followed by double-precision searches reportedly produced apparent nonzero feasible candidates on the reconstructed unrestricted grids. These checks suggest numerical sensitivity in selected cases; they do not resolve the remaining 592 cases or certify continuum feasibility.' Supply accepted-case counts, seeds, grids, solver tolerances, nonzero witnesses, and residuals. Describe walk records as correlated states, potentially repeated, rather than independent distinct boxes.

items.claim: Additional finding — Numerical routines do not implement the claimed feasibility decisions
items.objection: [closed_limit.py:130](/Users/jinleic/jinleic-workspace/ai4s/robust-spr-interval-synthesis/work/closed_limit.py:130) equates every nonzero solver status with infeasibility, although numerical failures and limits are different outcomes. Conversely, status zero can accompany a negative margin because s is allowed to be negative. In closed_exact3.py:139–142, λ = 0 and s = 0 are always feasible, so the LP optimum is always nonnegative in exact arithmetic. An optimum of zero does not prove existence of a nonzero closed solution: R = [I;−I] is an exact counterexample. Lines 144–155 give a sphere scan and local refinement, not a certified global maximum; a negative returned value therefore cannot prove infeasibility. The coefficient restriction in closed_limit.py needs qualification: it is justifiable for genuine closed solutions if the box contains a Hurwitz denominator, but that auxiliary fact is not stated or proved by the routine.
items.fix: Separate solver completion, witness feasibility, and certified infeasibility. For an unrestricted three-dimensional cone, use six exhaustive normalization charts λ_q = ±1 with |λ_j| ≤ 1 and Rλ ≥ 0; obtain exact witnesses or exact infeasibility certificates in every chart. Prove contact rank before claiming that this is the entire nullspace. Alternatively, justify the coefficient restriction by proving that a Hurwitz member makes β/a a nonnegative-real proper stable rational function, forcing every nonzero closed β to have nonnegative coefficients and positive coefficient sum. Validate witnesses against the original constraints; use exact polynomial nonnegativity checks before claiming results on the whole half-axis.

status_scoping_issues: The Lean statements faithfully encode monic, exact-degree, finite-frequency strict SPR; their compilation and transitive axiom audits were not reproduced.
The permitted sources support reported degree-five and degree-six results, not an exhaustive current-literature determination for every individual n ≥ 7.
Arbitrary-order polynomial-segment results do not settle interval boxes with independently varying coefficients.
The non-monic variant requires simultaneous synthesis on both normalized faces; individual monic synthesis results are insufficient.
Fully closed, nondegenerate marginal boxes are a selected boundary class. No theorem here makes them exhaustive for arbitrary synthesis failure.
Closed feasibility, nonzero grid feasibility, and exact-degree strict SPR synthesis are different conclusions.
overclaims: Root-band alternation alone is equivalent to robust Hurwitz stability.
Every marginal limit has n−2 distinct double contacts and a three-dimensional numerator space.
The sextic auxiliary odd bounds are literally the original interval endpoints.
All sampled closed problems were feasible despite 632 negative margins and only 40 rechecks.
The feasibility optimization was performed entirely in 60-digit arithmetic.
All floating-point negatives were proved to be conditioning artifacts.
Solver success, a zero LP margin, or a negative local sphere-search value constitutes a feasibility or infeasibility certificate.
best_next_step: Prove an exhaustive degree-seven first-failure reduction, extending the quintic manuscript's Proposition 3.3: derive the complete finite critical contact system for an arbitrary full-width stable box, with at most eight support functionals, retaining origin, infinity, degree-loss, and coincident-frequency cases. Establish precisely when Lemma B's eight-node alternation follows and characterize the remaining possibilities. This supplies a complete algebraic target for exclusion or an exact stable counterexample; the fully closed random searches currently lack that exhaustiveness.
